# ggplot3d

*three-dimensional plots with ggplot2*

![Height bands of the Maunga Whau volcano every 10 metres, from blue at
90 metres through beige to red at 200 metres, drawn as a flat ggplot2
contour map on the left and, with coord_3d(), draped over the shaded
volcano surface on the right.](reference/figures/ggplot3d-hero.svg)

ggplot3d draws three-dimensional points, paths, surfaces and solids with
[ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/).

The package extends ggplot2’s grammar of graphics with a z position
scale and a camera. Each panel combines its layers into a scene, the
collection of geometry used to determine which parts are visible. You
can map variables to position, colour and fill, choose a view, and save
the plot with
[`ggsave()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggsave.html).

ggplot3d supports:

- Surfaces with observations, contours and fitted values.
- Columns, extruded polygons and indexed meshes.
- Continuous, discrete and date/time z scales, including transformations
  and facets.
- Vector drawing and raster rendering from the same scene geometry.

[Visibility](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/vignettes/visibility.Rmd)
explains how overlapping geometry is ordered and split. The examples
below generate their figures from the package.

## Installation

The development version compiles C++17 code. Install build tools for
your operating system:

| Operating system | Build tools |
|----|----|
| Windows | [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) matching your R version |
| macOS | Run `xcode-select --install` in Terminal |
| Debian / Ubuntu | Install `r-base-dev` |

Check that R can find the compiler:

``` r

pkgbuild::has_build_tools(debug = TRUE)
```

Install the development package:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/ggplot3d")
```

## Usage

1.  Map three position columns with
    [`aes()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/aes.html).
2.  Add a three-dimensional layer and
    [`coord_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/coord_3d.md).

The data below contain a regular grid of x and y positions and a height
z. A surface connects neighbouring grid positions. The point layer marks
selected positions above and below that surface.

``` r

library(ggplot2)
library(ggplot3d)

surface <- expand.grid(x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 15),
                       y = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 15))
surface$z <- with(surface, exp(-(x^2 + y^2) / 2))
observations <- surface[c(49, 73, 97, 121, 145, 169), ]
observations$z <- observations$z + c(0.3, -0.3, 0.3, -0.3, 0.3, -0.3)

ggplot(surface, aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E") +
  geom_point_3d(data = observations, colour = "#B5342B", size = 3) +
  coord_3d()
```

![A curved blue surface with red observations above and below it,
partially hidden by the
surface.](reference/figures/README-surface-points-1.svg)

The result is a ggplot object. Layer geometry is depth-sorted together
within the panel, including where the surface covers a point.

## Intersecting surfaces

Each surface has its own data and fill. Their intersection determines
which pieces are visible from the chosen camera.

``` r

first <- surface
first$z <- with(first, 0.6 * x)
second <- surface
second$z <- with(second, -0.6 * x + 0.2 * y)

ggplot(first, aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E") +
  geom_surface_3d(data = second, fill = "#9E5E0F") +
  coord_3d(azimuth = -45, elevation = 60)
```

![Blue and orange sloping surfaces intersect along their
middle.](reference/figures/README-intersections-1.svg)

## Columns

Map z to the top of each column. The default baseline is zero; `zmin`
supplies a baseline from the data.

``` r

columns <- expand.grid(x = 1:3, y = 1:3)
columns$z <- c(2, 4, 3, 5, 2, 4, 3, 6, 2)

ggplot(columns, aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_col_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E", width = 0.65, depth = 0.65) +
  coord_3d()
```

![Nine blue columns on a three-by-three grid with different
heights.](reference/figures/README-columns-1.svg)

## Raster output

A raster backend draws the scene into pixels at the requested
resolution. It is useful for dense geometry and fixed-size images. Set
it inside the coordinate system.

``` r

raster_plot <- ggplot(surface, aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E") +
  geom_point_3d(data = observations, colour = "#B5342B", size = 3) +
  coord_3d(backend = backend_3d("raster", dpi = 144, antialias = 2))
raster_plot
```

![A raster rendering of the curved blue surface and red
observations.](reference/figures/README-raster-1.svg)

``` r

ggsave("surface.png", raster_plot, width = 5, height = 4.5, dpi = 144)
```

## Documentation

Start with [Get
started](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/vignettes/ggplot3d.Rmd) to
create and save a plot.

- [The z
  scale](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/vignettes/z-scale.Rmd):
  transformations, categories, limits and facets.
- [Layers](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/vignettes/layers.Rmd):
  points, paths, gridded surfaces, columns, distributions and intervals.
- [Surfaces, solids and
  fields](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/vignettes/surfaces-solids.Rmd):
  meshes, fitted and level surfaces, hulls, solid glyphs and sweeps.
- [Camera and
  framing](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/vignettes/camera.Rmd):
  view angles, projections and plot bounds.
- [Output
  backends](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/vignettes/backends.Rmd):
  choose vector or raster rendering.
- [Visibility](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/vignettes/visibility.Rmd):
  how the scene resolves overlapping geometry.

Function help is available in R, for example
[`?coord_3d`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/coord_3d.md)
and
[`?geom_surface_3d`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_surface_3d.md).

## Getting help

Send questions and bug reports to [GitHub
issues](https://github.com/gcol33/ggplot3d/issues). Include a small
reproducible example, the rendering backend, and
[`sessionInfo()`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/sessionInfo.html).

## Contributing

See [Contributing](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/CONTRIBUTING.md)
for development setup and documentation checks.

# Package index

## Spherical geometry and observers

- [`coord_spherical_geometry_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/coord_spherical_geometry_3d.md)
  : Spherical geometry in stereographic and gnomonic charts
- [`stat_hopf_fibre_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_hopf_fibre_3d.md)
  : Hopf fibres, latitude tori and their spherical base

## Tilings and honeycombs

- [`stat_tiling_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_tiling_3d.md)
  [`stat_honeycomb_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_tiling_3d.md)
  : Regular tilings and honeycombs from Coxeter reflections
- [`stat_project_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_project_3d.md)
  : Project four-dimensional and higher-dimensional data into three
  dimensions
- [`rotate_4d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/rotate_4d.md)
  : Rotations in four dimensions
- [`tour_grand()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/tour_grand.md)
  : Grand tours of three-dimensional projections
- [`stat_section_4d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_section_4d.md)
  : Hyperplane sections of four-dimensional tetrahedral meshes

## Hyperbolic geometry and data

- [`coord_hyperbolic_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/coord_hyperbolic_3d.md)
  : Finite hyperbolic ball and sheet coordinates
- [`stat_tree_hyperbolic_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_tree_hyperbolic_3d.md)
  : Deterministic tree layouts in hyperbolic space
- [`hyperbolic_focus_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/hyperbolic_focus_3d.md)
  : Focus paths for a hyperbolic embedding

## Relativity

- [`stat_light_cone_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_light_cone_3d.md)
  : Light cones and surfaces of constant spacetime interval
- [`stat_embedding_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_embedding_3d.md)
  : Schwarzschild spatial embedding diagram
- [`stat_geodesic_ode_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_geodesic_ode_3d.md)
  : Equatorial Schwarzschild spacetime geodesics
- [`lorentz_boost_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/lorentz_boost_3d.md)
  : Lorentz boosts in canonical coordinates
- [`coord_spacetime_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/coord_spacetime_3d.md)
  : Finite Minkowski spacetime coordinates

## Complex analysis

- [`mobius()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/mobius.md) :
  Mobius transformations of complex numbers, spheres and half-space
- [`stat_riemann_sphere_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_riemann_sphere_3d.md)
  : Domain colouring on the Riemann sphere
- [`stat_riemann_surface_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_riemann_surface_3d.md)
  : Riemann surfaces parametrised by an inverse function

## Immersed surfaces and knots

- [`stat_self_intersection_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_self_intersection_3d.md)
  : Transverse intersection curves of a triangle mesh
- [`stat_immersed_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_immersed_3d.md)
  : Immersed surface examples
- [`stat_knot_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_knot_3d.md)
  : Torus knots and knot tubes

## Coordinates and lighting

- [`coord_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/coord_3d.md)
  : Exact three-dimensional panel coordinates
- [`camera_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/camera_3d.md)
  : Named camera views
- [`facet_views()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/facet_views.md)
  : Show one 3D scene from several views
- [`stereo_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stereo_3d.md)
  : Stereo output for 3D panels
- [`light_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/light_3d.md)
  : Lighting for a 3D scene
- [`lights_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/lights_3d.md)
  : Combine lights for a 3D scene
- [`light_directional()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/light_directional.md)
  [`light_point()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/light_directional.md)
  [`light_head()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/light_directional.md)
  [`light_hemisphere()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/light_directional.md)
  : Lights for a 3D scene
- [`material_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/material_3d.md)
  : Surface materials
- [`shadow_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/shadow_3d.md)
  : Planar cast shadows
- [`depth_cue_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/depth_cue_3d.md)
  : Depth cues: fog, line width and eye-dome lighting
- [`clip_plane_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/clip_plane_3d.md)
  : Clipping planes

## Curvilinear and compositional frames

- [`coord_cylindrical_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/coord_cylindrical_3d.md)
  : Cylindrical three-dimensional coordinates
- [`coord_spherical_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/coord_spherical_3d.md)
  : Spherical three-dimensional coordinates
- [`coord_globe_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/coord_globe_3d.md)
  : Longitude, latitude and height on a globe
- [`coord_ternary_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/coord_ternary_3d.md)
  : Ternary prism coordinates
- [`coord_simplex_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/coord_simplex_3d.md)
  : Quaternary simplex coordinates

## Point, path and polygon layers

  : Point, path, segment, text and polygon layers in three dimensions
- [`geom_label_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_label_3d.md)

  : Labels with boxes and labels that repel each other
- [`geom_band_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_band_3d.md)
  : Draw a three-dimensional ribbon or wall
- [`geom_boxplot_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_boxplot_3d.md)
  [`geom_violin_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_boxplot_3d.md)
  : Boxplots and violins standing on an x/y plane
- [`geom_area_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_area_3d.md)
  [`geom_waterfall_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_area_3d.md)
  : Filled area walls and waterfall curtains
- [`geom_dropline_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_dropline_3d.md)
  : Drop segments from points to a box face
- [`geom_quiver_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_quiver_3d.md)
  [`geom_cone_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_quiver_3d.md)
  : Vector fields with solid cone heads
- [`geom_rug_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_rug_3d.md)
  : Rug ticks on the walls of the panel box
- [`geom_plane_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_plane_3d.md)
  : Reference planes
- [`annotate_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/annotate_3d.md)
  : Annotations with a height
- [`geom_refline_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_refline_3d.md)
  [`geom_abline_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_refline_3d.md)
  : Reference lines through the panel box
- [`geom_bracket_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/geom_bracket_3d.md)
  : Brackets and dimension lines between two points

## Interval layers

  : Stems from a base value to each point
- [`stat_summary_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_summary_3d.md)
  : Summarise one axis at each position on the other two

  : Small multiples on parallel planes

## Images and textures

  : Images for textured faces

  : An image on a plane of the panel

# Articles

### Concepts

- [The z scale](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/z-scale.md):

- [Layers](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/layers.md):

  Worked examples of points, paths, gridded surfaces, columns,
  distributions, intervals and reference geometry.

- [Surfaces, solids and
  fields](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/surfaces-solids.md):

  Worked examples of indexed meshes, function and fitted surfaces,
  density surfaces, level surfaces, hulls, solid glyphs and sweeps along
  curves.

### Workflows

- [Camera and
  framing](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/camera.md):

  Set camera angles, projection, framing and stereo output for static
  scenes.

- [Output
  backends](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/backends.md):

  Choose vector, raster, hybrid or traced rendering and save figures at
  the intended resolution.

- [Lighting and surface
  styles](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/lighting.md):

- [Ray marching and
  volumes](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/ray-marching.md):

  Trace signed distance surfaces, integrate scalar volumes and
  accumulate seeded path-traced images.

- [Interactive
  viewing](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/viewer.md):

  Explore WebGL 2 scenes with tooltips, picking, selection, linked
  cameras and crosstalk filters.

- [Exporting plots and
  scenes](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/export.md):

  Write model files, animated glTF, semantic SVG, TikZ and Asymptote, or
  pass scenes to rgl and rayrender.

- [Camera animation and
  interaction](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/motion.md):

  Render camera moves, tween points and surfaces between data states,
  and explore linked interactive panels.

- [Combining 2D and 3D
  graphics](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/combining-2d-3d.md):

  Place ggplot2 panels on walls, stack slices in depth, draw terraced
  contours and arrange 2D and 3D plots.

- [Documents](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/documents.md):

  Use knitr and Quarto to choose HTML viewers or static figures, supply
  alt text and compose panels.

- [Maps and spatial
  data](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/spatial.md):

  Draw raster terrain, simple features and XYZ geometry, prism maps,
  profiles, flow arcs and space-time paths.

- [Vector
  fields](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/vector-fields.md):

  Draw vector arrows, magnitude-scaled cones, integrated streamlines and
  solid streamtubes from a gridded field.

### Examples

- [Gallery](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/gallery.md):

  Worked plots of solid curves, distributions, covariance ellipsoids,
  streamtubes, cutaways and contour terraces alongside familiar charts.

- [Linear and nonlinear
  PDEs](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/pde.md):

  Exact solutions of four linear and four nonlinear partial differential
  equations drawn as surfaces that change over time with animate_3d().

- [Implicit
  surfaces](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/implicit-surfaces.md):

  Draw level sets from functions, reconstruct surfaces from point clouds
  and triangulate scattered height measurements.

- [Inside the Thurston
  geometries](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/thurston-geometries.md):

  Render an observer view in each of the eight Thurston geometries using
  intrinsic balls and geodesics.

- [Tensor
  glyphs](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/tensors.md):
